title: A store that refuses stale saves

blocks.text: The school district's (invented for this practice) facility planners edit repair plans from several laptops at once. A plan is a dict such as `{"roofs": 400, "boilers": 250}`. Two planners who read the same plan and both save would lose one of the two changes, so the store keeps a version number per plan, starting at 1.

items: `read(plan_id)` returns the plan and its version. A caller may change the dict it gets back as much as it likes; that must not change the stored plan.

`save(plan_id, read_version, plan)` stores `plan` and returns the new version, one more than before, if the plan is still at `read_version`. Otherwise it returns `None` and stores nothing. A caller who keeps changing its dict after a save must not change the stored plan either.

cases.says: a save made from the current version is stored and returns the next version
the second of two saves made from the same read is refused and the first one's change survives
changing the dict that read returned does not change the stored plan
changing a dict after saving it does not change the stored plan

origin.section: A Write Names the Version It Read, and a Stale Write Is Refused

concepts: a save names the version it read and is refused when that version is no longer current
